name: notecom
description: Web-based lesson library: plain-language study notes generated from slides/PDFs by Claude Code, read and managed by a Next.js app in a code-editor-style viewer.
purpose: Notes are written in plain high-school-level language with technically correct terminology (Information Systems & Network Engineering program). Content creation happens entirely outside the web application — Claude Code is the sole author; the Next.js app is the reader/manager.
principles: Claude Code authors content as files; the Next.js app reads and manages it in Supabase. Claude Code is the author but is not a layer inside the app.
Supabase is the source of truth. No local database, no sync worker, no per-instance state.
Naming/slug/sequence logic lives in the app (lib/vault/slug.ts, the generated index.json) — every value reaches the database fully resolved.
No content persistence from a React component or API route directly — always through lib/vault/store.ts.
The app writes no files. vault/ is generation output, ingested one-way by lib/vault/import.ts.
No AI generation logic or Anthropic API calls in the Next.js app itself; one sanctioned delegation exists (the generation job runner).
Retrieval and ranking live in SQL (notes_search_chunks, notes_related_docs), not in TypeScript.
Authorization is Row Level Security. No service-role key exists anywhere in this app; every query carries the caller's JWT.
No business logic in the desktop shell (Tauri) — only start/stop orchestration.

webapp.role: UI, routing, API handlers, content management (create/rename/delete/list) against Supabase

delegations.name: Generate from file
delegations.mechanism: spawns local Claude Code CLI headlessly (-p, --output-format stream-json)

dataLayer.role: all content persistence; no permission logic of its own
dataLayer.client: user-scoped Supabase client (anon key + caller's JWT)

vaultImport.role: one-way ingest of Claude-authored vault files into Supabase

search.role: section chunking in the app, ranking in Postgres
search.storage: notes_doc_chunks (generated tsvector + GIN index; derived, rebuildable from notes_documents.html)
search.queryParser: websearch_to_tsquery('simple', q) — bare words are ANDed

desktop.role: Tauri shell: orchestration only, no business logic
desktop.vaultLocation: checkout's vault/, baked in at compile time (single-vault, checkout-centric design)

storageModel.sourceOfTruth: Supabase Postgres (notes_folders, notes_documents; notes_doc_chunks is the derived search index)

local-desktop.description: Tauri native window; one Node process, reading and writing Supabase directly
local-desktop.command: npm run dev:desktop | npm run build:desktop

local-browser.description: plain Next.js dev/prod server on the writer machine, full read/write + generation
local-browser.command: npm run dev | npm run build && npm run start

vps.description: single stateless web container behind a reverse proxy; identical app, no local vault, so no generation
requires: SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY at build time (NEXT_PUBLIC_* are inlined into the client bundle)
cannotRunRemotely: /api/generate (requires a local claude CLI signed in to that person's own subscription)

techStack.auth: Supabase accounts (password + emailed code); RLS is the authorization boundary; no service-role key
techStack.dataLayer: lib/vault/store.ts over a user-scoped Supabase client

outOfScope: No offline mode — every read and write goes to Supabase as it happens
No anonymous access — anon is granted nothing on any notes_* table
No per-document permissions — folders are the unit of sharing
No AI generation logic inside the application itself
No hosting/deployment pipeline beyond what's documented in README.md and docs/deploy-vps.md
